claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.text: Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me first read the official eligibility rules so I can assist you properly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. I've reviewed the Child Benefit eligibility rules. To help determine if you're eligible, I'll need to ask you some questions.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have a son, Alex. He's 17 and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to understand his current situation.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in approved education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Let me ask a follow-up question about Alex's current situation.

Has Alex started paid work for 24 hours or more a week, or is he receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work that much - he's not doing 24 hours a week or anything like that. And he's not getting any benefits in his own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment.

First, do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or does anyone else also consider themselves responsible for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. It's just me - he lives with me and I'm responsible for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. Let me also confirm - are there any special circumstances, such as Alex being in hospital, care, or residential accommodation for an extended period?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. He's just at home with me, no hospital stays or care arrangements or anything.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for answering all my questions. Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why: While you meet many of the basic requirements (you live in the UK, Alex lives with you, you're responsible for him, and no one else is claiming for him), the key issue is Alex's age and status.

Since Alex is 17 (over 16 years old), you can only continue to receive Child Benefit if he is in **approved education or training**. As Alex is not currently in approved education or training, you don't qualify for Child Benefit for him.

**However**, if Alex's circumstances change and he:
- Returns to approved education or training (and is under 20), or
- Registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services after leaving education (which can extend Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks for 16 or 17 year olds)

Then you may become eligible to claim Child Benefit at that point. If his situation does change, you would need to contact the Child Benefit Office to update them.
